# SK9016 — Applying the canonical changes a `dotnet_diagnostic` severity

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

Applying the canonical would change one or more `dotnet_diagnostic.<id>.severity` values, measured as effective value against effective value with the local block laid over the incoming payload. Warning when it moves a compiler diagnostic (`CS…`, `BC…`) up to `warning` or `error`, or newly sets one there; info when it lowers or drops a compiler severity, and info for analyzer severities in either direction. `skala config diff --canonical` lists every change before you apply it; `config sync` prints the summary before it writes.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Compilation |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Under `TreatWarningsAsErrors` a compiler severity raised by an `.editorconfig` commit is a build failure from a change that touches no code — it took one repository from 0 errors to 17. `SK9013` reports overrides for keys the option registry owns, and `dotnet_diagnostic` keys are deliberately not in it, so until this id existed the loudest thing the canonical could do to a repository was the one thing it did silently. A lowered severity is the widest kind of suppression there is (docs/plan/09 § "--no-new-suppressions"), so that direction is reported too, at info. To keep a severity the canonical would move, pin it below `# skala:local begin`: the local block wins and the change stops being reported.

## When it does not fire

⚠ The warning form cannot fire on the shipped canonical today: the template carries zero `dotnet_diagnostic` assignments, and a test holds that count at zero so an export cannot bring them back unnoticed. It is reachable with a custom or older payload. A key the local block already pins is not counted, and a stricter local `error` is not reported as lowered by a canonical `warning`. A severity the file does not set at all is reported as introduced rather than raised, because the compiler default it moves away from is written in no `.editorconfig` and Skala does not invent a table of them.
